neighbours.label: the head noun (or its first piece) after a run of descriptive adjectives ('thick yellow first milk', 'bright, urgent main passages')
fire: We walked through a cold, damp, ancient forest at dawn.
She wore a long, flowing, dark blue dress to the gala.
The old man told a slow, strange, haunting story by the fire.
They rented a small, bright, cozy apartment near the river.
A loud, sharp, metallic noise came from the engine.
He bought a sleek, shiny, expensive watch for his father.
The chef served a rich, creamy, buttery sauce with the fish.
Ein warmer, weicher, frischer Kuchen stand auf dem Tisch.
quiet: We walked through the forest at dawn with our dogs.
She wore the dress to the gala and danced all night.
The old man told the story by the fire after dinner.
They rented the apartment near the river last spring.
The noise came from the engine when it started.
He bought the watch for his father on Sunday.
The chef served the sauce with the fish at noon.
Der Kuchen stand seit dem Morgen auf dem Tisch.

notes: Top examples peak on the noun after stacked adjectives, in English and German. Probe: 'The thick, golden, sticky honey' 0.24 vs 'The honey dripped' 0.002. Near misses: the same nouns with no adjectives before them.
